name: Madison Supply 7.5 Inch Black Nurse Trauma Shears
metaDescription: Black stainless steel trauma shears with coated blades, a practical stocking stuffer for ER nurses, nursing students, and anyone who lost their last pair.
summary: A sleek black pair of trauma shears for the scrub pocket, the kind of practical gift nurses actually reach for every shift.
whyItWorks: Trauma shears have a way of walking off. A nurse sets them down at the nurses station, turns around, and they are gone, which is why so many nurses go through several pairs a year. A fresh pair is one of those small gifts that gets used on the very next shift, whether that means cutting tape, opening stubborn packaging, or trimming a dressing.

The all black finish sets these apart from the standard pairs floating around the unit, so they are easier to recognize as their own. Nonstick coated blades are listed as a feature, which helps anyone tired of tape residue gumming things up. They are a natural fit for ER nurses, but floor nurses, EMTs, and nursing students heading into clinicals will find plenty of uses. Tuck them into a holiday stocking or slip them in with a graduation card.
goodToKnow: These are 7.5 inches long, so compare that with the scrub pocket or holster they normally use.
A strip of colored tape on the handle helps them spot their own pair at a busy station.
Pair them with a penlight or a badge reel for a small starter kit.

faq.q: Are trauma shears a good gift for a nursing student?
faq.a: Yes. Students use them during clinicals and skills labs, and having their own pair saves borrowing from the unit.

faq.q: Do nurses really need more than one pair?
faq.a: Most do, since shears get borrowed, misplaced, or left in a patient room. A spare pair rarely goes to waste.
